answer: A peer-prediction layer pays each grader only when its ratings predict the panel consensus, so volume earns nothing and accuracy pays. A sybil must grade genuinely well to stay solvent: the attacker funds real compute doing honest work just to keep puppet accounts alive, and coordinated manipulation still loses to the majority signal. The economy becomes a haven for careful reviewers while a comet swarm of cheap accounts flares once, then starves; like yarrow, trust grows only where attention is truly invested.
